title: Algebraization of a formal glueing datum
statement: Let $R,S$ be commutative rings, $\varphi:R\to S$ a flat ring map [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], $t\in\mathbf N$, $f:\operatorname{Fin}(t)\to R$, and $I=(f_i)_i$, and suppose $R/I\to S/IS$ is bijective. Let $\mathrm{Can}:\mathrm{Mod}_R\to\mathrm{Glue}(\varphi,f)$ be a functor whose object at every $M$ has prime module $S\otimes_R M$, chart modules $M_{f_i}$, and actual canonical structural maps $c^M_{f_i},\sigma^M_{f_i,f_j}$, identified by bundled equalities and heterogeneous equalities [def-weil-pbc-formal-glueing-data], [def-weil-module-base-change], [def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away]. For every glueing datum $X$ there exists an $R$-module $E$ and an isomorphism $\mathrm{Can}(E)\cong X$. This asserts only essential surjectivity, with no assumption on Can on morphisms and no assertion about its Hom maps.

source.place: More on Algebra, Proposition 05ER, second and third paragraphs of the proof; steps 7–11 of prop-weil-pbc-formal-glueing-equivalence.

proof.text: Obtain H and a morphism psi : Can(H) -> X with injective prime component, bijective charts, and ideal-power torsion prime cokernel from the injective-approximation theorem.

Let U be the range of psi prime and Q the restriction to R of X prime/U. Transport the domain of psi prime to S tensor H using the given object equality, obtaining an injective iota. The quotient map rho gives an exact pair iota,rho and is surjective. The torsion-module comparison and tensor commutation make x -> 1 tensor x bijective. Define the S-linear multiplication map mu : S tensor Q -> Q by s tensor x -> s x. Since mu(1 tensor x)=x and every tensor is of that form, mu is bijective. Its inverse composed with rho is an S-linear surjection pi : X prime -> S tensor Q and forms an exact pair with iota.

The ideal generated by the finite family f is finitely generated. Apply the torsion-extension descent theorem to iota and pi. Obtain E, an injective j : H -> E, an exact pair j,q with quotient Q, and theta : S tensor E -> X prime satisfying theta composed with S tensor j = iota. The universes of H and Q are max(u,v,w), so the descended E also lies in that universe.

Localization preserves injectivity of j and exactness of j,q. For each generator f_i and localized element x/d of E, a power f_i^n kills q(x), since f_i^n belongs to I^n. The fraction equality criterion then shows q(x)/d=0. Localized exactness gives a preimage under j_fi, so j_fi is surjective and hence bijective. Apply extension transport with psi,j,theta to get a morphism Phi : Can(E) -> X with every component bijective.

Take the linear inverses of each component of Phi. Functoriality of localization and base change sends their two inverse identities to inverse identities. Compose the two compatibility squares with these inverses to obtain the inverse morphism of glueing data. Componentwise composition is identity in both directions; proof irrelevance handles the compatibility fields. These maps form the requested isomorphism Can(E) ~= X.

lean.statement:
theorem canonical_essentially_surjective {R : Type u} {S : Type v}
    [CommRing R] [CommRing S] (φ : R →+* S) (t : ℕ) (f : Fin t → R)
    (Can : ModuleCat.{max u v w} R ⥤ Data.{u, v, max u v w} φ f)
    (hobj : (∀ M : ModuleCat.{max u v w} R,
        (Can.obj M).M' = extend φ M ∧
        (∀ i : Fin t, (Can.obj M).M i =
          ModuleCat.of (Localization.Away (f i)) (LocalizedModule.Away (f i) M)) ∧
        (∀ i : Fin t, HEq ((Can.obj M).alpha i).toLinearMap (compare φ (f i) M)) ∧
        (∀ i j : Fin t,
          HEq ((Can.obj M).alpha_overlap i j).toLinearMap (swap (f i) (f j) M))))
    (hflat : φ.Flat)
    (hquot : Function.Bijective
      (Ideal.quotientMap ((Ideal.span (Set.range f)).map φ) φ Ideal.le_comap_map))
    (X : Data.{u, v, max u v w} φ f) :
    ∃ M : ModuleCat.{max u v w} R, Nonempty (Can.obj M ≅ X)
